agent_notes: Change type: a control-tightening change that only affects logging. It wraps three DEBUG log arguments (add_file, remove_file, update_file) in the existing shared helper common.sanitize_log_value, which the controller.py log sites in commit 45ff4bd already use.

Public API: no signatures changed. Model.add_file, remove_file and update_file keep the same parameters, return values and exceptions (the ModelError messages are unchanged and still do not include the filename). All 25 importers listed (controller, auto_queue, extract dispatch/process, file_operation_manager, model_builder, web stream_model/serialize_model, and tests) are unaffected.
Import safety: common/__init__.py line 1 re-exports sanitize_log_value from .types. model.py already imported AppError from common, so this adds no new import cycle or package dependency.

Type safety: the helper calls value.replace(...), so it needs a str. file.name is a ModelFile name (str), and remove_file(filename) is keyed by the same str names used in self.__files. If a caller passed a non-str name it would already fail the dict lookup semantics. No new crash path was found.

Behavior change visible to operators: DEBUG log lines for filenames that contain control characters now show escaped tokens (\n, \r, \xHH) instead of the raw bytes. Any log grep or alerting that matched raw control characters in these three DEBUG lines would change, which is unlikely and only at DEBUG level. C1 and non-ASCII Unicode filenames pass through unchanged, so normal international filenames look the same.
Schema/DB/migration: none. Model state is in memory only, and nothing is persisted or serialized differently. serialize_model and stream_model read ModelFile objects, not log output.

Blast radius: limited to the text of 3 DEBUG log lines in one module. If the helper had a bug, the worst case would be an exception raised inside add/remove/update before the model mutates. That would affect the controller scan loop, but the helper is simple, pure and already tested by its existing callers.
Verdict: shippable as-is. No blocking issues; the only finding is a negligible performance note.

findings.fix_hint: Optional: switch to lazy %-style logging (self.logger.debug("... '%s'", sanitize_log_value(...))) or guard with logger.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG); not required.
findings.problem: The debug log lines build their message with str.format(), so sanitize_log_value(file.name) runs on every add_file, remove_file and update_file call, even when the logger is above DEBUG. sanitize_log_value (src/python/common/types.py:45-58) makes two str.replace passes and then loops over every character in Python. The old code also built the message regardless of log level, so the only new cost is one O(len(name)) scan per call. Filenames are short and model mutations only happen for files that changed in a scan cycle, so the overhead should be negligible. pending: profiling a model rebuild with thousands of changed files would show whether this cost is measurable.

findings.why_it_matters: Model mutations run on the controller's scan loop thread. Extra work there scales with the number of changed files per cycle, but it is a few microseconds per call.
